STYLE BLOCK 8.
Rendering: an expressive editorial cartoon caricature with believable adult anatomy and complete, well-observed clothing. Use flat cel shading and thin, precise pen contours. Preserve the garment construction and footwear detail. Simplify tonal rendering, not the identity or the objects. This is a satirical cartoon, not a minimalist icon or a realistic portrait.
Caricature: use the height, the head size, and the build that this prompt gives. Keep the complete head, hair, ears, and chin inside the stated head-height limits. Preserve individual identity through observed facial shapes and expression, with restrained exaggeration of named features. Do not turn the face into a geometric mask or a mascot. Each body is adult.
Face: use natural adult facial proportions and anatomical detail within the stated head size. Draw believable eyelids, modest almond-shaped eyes, simple irises and pupils, restrained brows, the nose bridge and nostrils, natural lips, cheek contours, ears, and age-appropriate expression lines. Keep individual asymmetry and character. Use one flat skin base color without portrait shading, skin highlights, blush, or tonal modeling. Explain facial structure with purposeful linework, not oversized eyes, thick geometric eyebrows, a button nose, an oversized jaw, or a broad generic grin. Use no pores, iris texture, stubble dots, or photographic skin detail.
Hair: use one solid silhouette and at most one broad hard-edged shadow shape. Use the same rule for facial hair. Use no strands, streaks, thin bands, or separate highlights.
Contours: draw a single thin, clean, continuous dark pen outline. Do not inherit a heavier outline from an input image and do not add a second stroke around an existing stroke. Target 4.1 source pixels per 1000 pixels of reference height, with accepted figure and body-part medians from 3.90 through 4.20. Reference height is 94 percent of the canvas height. At 1254 pixels square, the nominal stroke is 4.83 source pixels, with accepted medians from 4.60 through 4.95. Keep this narrow stroke consistent around the head, arms, torso, and legs for every height and build. Preserve all thinner interior garment and facial lines. Use no bold outer ink, sticker border, double outline, broken, sketchy, tapered, or colored outline.
Shading: each clothing or shoe material uses one flat base color and one hard-edged shadow tone. That shadow tone may form several distinct regions to explain folds and construction. Keep each region flat. Do not replace useful contour and fold lines with tonal modeling. Shoes, lenses, and metal fittings may have a small flat highlight. Use no gradients, airbrush, photographic texture, fabric weave, rim light, or glow.
Detail: retain jacket lapels, seams, visible buttons and buttonholes, pockets, shirt collar and placket, and cuffs. When the brief specifies a belt, show its band and buckle at the waistband. Draw anatomically and mechanically plausible trouser folds at the hips, crotch, knees, and ankles without an arbitrary fold-count limit. Construct shoes with a believable toe, vamp, laces and eyelets when specified, a distinct sole, and a heel. Keep these details readable and purposeful. Do not erase them to make the shading simpler. Use no microscopic stitching or decorative noise.
Not permitted: a realistic or semi-realistic face, lifelike skin, portrait lighting, painterly blending, a three-dimensional render, anime, a sticker border, or mixed rendering techniques.
